source.title: Reading Task Failure Off the Activations: A Sparse-Feature Audit of GPT-2 Small on Indirect Object Identification

page_placements.theme: IOI behaviour depends on wording and prompt format

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper audits SAE features and IOI behavior, but does not test the proposed attention-head circuit, its head classes, or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.gate_note: The authors discuss the established IOI circuit and report a feature-level audit, a single SAE-feature ablation, and IOI behavior across object choices and templates. These are not tests of the proposed 26-head circuit or its roles under patching. No cited results are recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study runs a layer-8 SAE-feature audit of GPT-2 small's IOI failures and measures behavioural accuracy across objects, templates and seeds. It never ablates, patches or identifies attention heads, so it tests no version. V1, V2 and V4 need head-level circuit tests. V3 needs other models. V5 needs evaluation of the circuit's faithfulness. V6 needs component-level evidence across prompt variants, and accuracy alone cannot show which components carry IOI. The authors call feature 10,036 'a small piece of corroborating evidence' for the name-mover story, but they did no head-to-feature attribution. It is not significant after Holm correction on the subset, so it is not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The 'the keys' behavioural effect is robust across seeds. The feature-level causal story fails all three controls (ablation, raw-residual baseline, seed robustness). The authors present the audit pipeline plus its controls as the contribution.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a layer-8 sparse-autoencoder feature audit, failure-prediction classifiers, and a single-feature SAE ablation. It does not use the original attention-head circuit discovery, head ablations, or patching tests.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI failure rate varies sharply with transferred-object wording: the “the keys” subset has a 93.3% failure rate in the seed-42 corpus versus 7.5% on the other seven objects. The specific top-|d| SAE feature also varies across seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2 small's IOI accuracy collapses when the transferred object is 'the keys': 93.3% failure vs 7.5% on the other objects. The effect holds across five seeds (75–93% failure), while the four templates differ from the overall rate by at most 4 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT-2 small's IOI behaviour is not invariant to transferred-object wording; some object tokens sharply degrade accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The top failure-correlated layer-8 SAE feature does not restore accuracy when ablated. Raw residual-stream probes match the SAE-feature probes (AUC 0.929 vs 0.927 for the top 100 features). The top feature changes across seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-feature correlates of IOI failure are not reliable causal explanations and are seed-sensitive.

record.problems: Evidence about the proposed attention-head circuit is absent: the study uses one model, one SAE, and one layer, and its ablation concerns a single SAE feature rather than circuit heads. The authors also note that the five-seed check is small, the feature interpretation relies on autogenerated labels and one human auditor, and the ablation does not rule out multi-feature, earlier-layer, or position-specific causes.
record.rows_left_out: None. The reported IOI behavior and feature-audit results bearing on the claim’s subject are included; no original-circuit result is reported.

Circuit faithfulness and completeness under different ablations, metrics and prompt distributions.
Whether the same circuit components carry IOI across templates and objects. Only behavioural accuracy is measured: templates are within 4 pp, and 'the keys' fails 93.3%.

record.verdict_notes: Only Section II-B and the Section IV-G remark mention the Wang et al. circuit. Section IV-G calls feature 10,036 consistent with a working name-mover circuit, but the authors explicitly have not done head-to-feature attribution. The keys effect is behaviour-only evidence. It may interest V6 curators as a prompt-variant sensitivity, but it does not show whether different components are used.

relation.reason: It discusses the established IOI circuit as background and offers tentative feature-level corroboration, but explicitly lacks head-to-feature attribution and does not test or use the identified circuit as an experimental tool.

tranche.reason: The study audits behavioural failures and SAE-feature correlates without testing the specified attention-head circuit, its self-repair, transfer, recovery across methods, or circuit evaluation sensitivity.

source_check.notes: Object-dependent behavioural accuracy does not establish different circuit components or heuristics. The authors distinguish the robust behavioural finding from the unsupported single-feature causal interpretation.
